title: Blind cast lets IPC registry drift reach runtime
reasoning: The renderer imports the shared IPC JSON and asserts it is a complete SharedChannelRegistry, so TypeScript will trust every listed channel key even if the JSON is missing, renamed, or has an unexpected value. A drifted entry would still compile, but consumers of INVOKE_CHANNELS/SEND_CHANNELS could receive undefined or a wrong channel string at runtime and then pass it into IpcBridge.invoke/send. In production, bridge validation is skipped, so the bad channel would be forwarded to window.ipc/preload instead of failing at module load with a clear parity error.
recommendation: Replace the unchecked cast with a small runtime shape check for the expected SEND_CHANNELS, INVOKE_CHANNELS, and ON_CHANNELS keys, or generate the TypeScript registry/types from the shared JSON so missing keys fail before release. Keep the validation local to this boundary so renderer callers cannot observe a partially invalid registry.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata includes no linked tests, and the package only exposes general Jest/typecheck scripts; the shown source has no regression test asserting the imported JSON contains every renderer-declared channel key.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Jest test for frontend/src/renderer/infrastructure/ipc/channels.ts that imports the channel module and asserts each expected registry key is present with the exact string value, plus a negative/unit test for the runtime validator if one is added.
minimumFixScope: frontend/src/renderer/infrastructure/ipc/channels.ts plus a focused frontend Jest test.
